text: State changes only re-run the specific code that depends on them, enabling fine-grained reactivity
quote: Declare your state and use it throughout your app, and when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it will rerun.

text: Built-in Context and Stores provide global state management without needing a third-party library
quote: Performant state management is built-in with Context and Stores: you don't have to reach for a third party library to manage global state

text: Resources let server-loaded data be treated as reactive state, paired with Suspense for responsive loading UIs
quote: With Resources, you can use data loaded from the server like any other piece of state and build a responsive UI for it thanks to Suspense and concurrent rendering.

text: Full server-side rendering support with streaming to speed up time-to-interactive
quote: Solid has full SSR and serverless support, with streaming and progressive hydration to get to interactive as quickly as possible.

text: Progressive hydration lets apps become interactive faster after server rendering
quote: Solid has full SSR and serverless support, with streaming and progressive hydration to get to interactive as quickly as possible.

text: Serverless deployment support for SSR apps
quote: Solid has full SSR and serverless support, with streaming and progressive hydration to get to interactive as quickly as possible.

text: Components render as real DOM nodes, so you can inspect and debug them directly in browser devtools
quote: A `<div>` is a real div, so you can use your browser's devtools to inspect the rendering

text: Custom renderers can be written to target platforms beyond the browser DOM
quote: Universal: write custom renderers to use Solid anywhere

text: Framework is friendly to web components and supports authoring custom elements
quote: Web component friendly and can author custom elements

text: Minimal abstraction gives direct DOM access, making it easy to integrate native JS libraries like D3
quote: Solid's bare-metal, minimal abstractions give you direct access to the DOM, making it easy to use your favorite native JavaScript libraries like D3.
